reasons: internal/proxy/tracking.go:231-248 handleMomentoProxy builds a fresh *http.Transport (and ReverseProxy) for every /momento/* request. A Transport keeps its keep-alive connection plus readLoop/writeLoop goroutines alive until the peer closes it (IdleConnTimeout is 0 on a custom Transport and CloseIdleConnections is never called), so every tracker.js fetch and every visitor beacon leaks one TCP connection to the collector and ~3 goroutines. Reproduced outside the repo with the identical pattern: 200 proxied requests -> goroutines 4 -> 604 after GC, none reclaimed. Under real visitor traffic this is an unbounded fd/goroutine leak on the success path. Fix: one shared Transport on the Server (or at least DisableKeepAlives/CloseIdleConnections). The proxy integration test (TestMomentoProxyForwardsSameOriginTraffic) cannot catch this because it makes only two requests.

internal/proxy/tracking.go:91 tracking.allowed_hosts is registered with no validator, and SplitHosts (internal/tracking/tracking.go:248-260) only splits on comma/whitespace, so whatever an operator types via PUT /admin/settings/by-key/tracking.allowed_hosts is spliced verbatim into script-src/connect-src/img-src (tracking.go:240-242, policy.go:54). Values such as 'unsafe-inline', *, data:, or https://a.example;default-src * pass straight into the Content-Security-Policy header of every /app page. This contradicts the commit message, the package doc (tracking.go:10), and ADMIN_GUIDE.md 3.6 ('never unsafe-inline' / 'widened by exactly those origins'). The /admin/tracking/violations/allow path validates strictly (tracking.go:313-318) but the ordinary settings write does not, so the documented invariant is unenforced on the path the runtime-settings tab actually uses.
notes: Tests are genuine: tracking package, appui injection, proxy integration and Vitest tab tests all exercise the new code and would fail on the pre-change code. go test ./internal/proxy ./internal/tracking ./internal/appui and vitest for the tab pass (OpenAPI snapshot included).

Commit message and ADMIN_GUIDE say 'every console page ships with script-src self', but the legacy /admin page has no Content-Security-Policy header at all and serveTrackedLegacyPage sets none; injection works there anyway, the description just overstates.

SnippetOrigins adds every http(s) URL found anywhere in a custom snippet (including comments/docs links) to script-src/connect-src/img-src — documented, but wider than 'exactly what the snippet needs'.
Tracked index.html (serveTrackedIndex) bypasses the gzip path used by serveFile; performance only.
Momento proxy forwards collector response headers (e.g. Set-Cookie) onto the gateway origin unchanged; minor given the collector is operator-controlled.
tracking.* settings fall into the 'admin' permission group; tracking.custom_snippet lets any full admin execute arbitrary JS in every user's /app session, comparable to the 'security' group settings.
ADMIN_GUIDE 3.6 says browsers send report-uri reports without credentials; same-origin report-uri POSTs do carry cookies. Harmless since the handler ignores them.
Rollback is clean: all settings default off, no migration; leftover tracking.* rows in admin_settings are ignored by older code.
